subject: Procurement channel recommendation for regulated workloads — marketplace vs direct
messages:
From: Tom Riley <tom.riley@medsynhealth.com>
To: elliot_price@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medsynhealth.com
Date: 2027-02-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Purchase options for patient-data workload (marketplace vs direct)

Hi Elliot,

We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will process de-identified patient telemetry and potentially PHI under a controlled environment. Procurement here asks whether they should pursue an AWS Marketplace private offer or go through a signed MSA/PO direct with Redwood. Key constraints:
- We need SOC2 + DPA in the contract;
- PO and AP team want cloud-billed invoices if possible (to charge back to the correct cost center);
- We may need to run Redwood Private in our VPC/on-prem later;
- Timeline: pilot needs to start in ~6 weeks, procurement lead time is usually ~8–10 weeks for direct MSAs.

Can you outline the tradeoffs so we can advise Procurement and Legal? Also, who on Redwood should procurement talk to about seller-of-record and billing sponsor mapping if we go marketplace?

Thanks — Tom
Tom Riley
Head of IT Operations, MedSyn Health
procurement@medsynhealth.com
From: elliot_price@redwood.ai
To: Tom Riley <tom.riley@medsynhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-11T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Purchase options for patient-data workload (marketplace vs direct)

Hi Tom — thanks for the clear constraints. High level guidance below, and I cc'd Ben (sales ops) for billing/PO details and Lauren (legal liaison) for contract/DPA routing.

Short answer: Marketplace private offers can often shorten procurement time and enable cloud billing, but they trade off on contractual flexibility (custom DPAs, indemnities, custom SLAs). Direct contracts (MSA + PO) give you full control over terms and are better if you anticipate on-prem/private deployments or stricter legal terms.

Tradeoffs (quick):
- Speed: Marketplace private offer > direct MSA (private offer can be completed in ~2–4 weeks if both sides accept the PO flow).
- Terms: Direct MSA allows custom DPA/SLA addenda; marketplace private offers typically require acceptance of the marketplace terms and have limited negotiation windows.
- Billing & Chargeback: Marketplace routes charges through the cloud provider (good for AP/chargeback). Direct invoice from Redwood fits vendors who prefer vendor invoices and direct net-30 POs.
- Seller of Record & Co-sell: If you want Redwood sales credit and co-sell motion with the cloud provider, we can map the seller-of-record and request co-sell tagging on the private offer, but that requires coordination with the cloud partner and may affect booking/crediting timelines.
- Private deployment: Direct contract is simpler if you plan to transition to Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) because we often need addenda for deployment responsibilities and acceptance criteria.

Next steps: Ben can propose two concrete paths (1) private offer + standard DPA addendum, and (2) direct MSA with a draft DPA. We should also schedule a short sync with your procurement/legal team. Attaching a sample SOW outline and marketplace guidance doc.

Best,
Elliot Price
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Tom Riley <tom.riley@medsynhealth.com>, elliot_price@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-12T08:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Purchase options for patient-data workload (marketplace vs direct)

Tom — quick operational notes from Finance/Sales Ops: 

If you lean marketplace private offer: 
- We can request an AWS Private Offer (PO flow) that invoices through AWS and shows up as an AWS line item for your cost center. That satisfies AP/cloud-billing requirements.
- We will need the billing sponsor and PO number up front. AWS typically requires the private offer created and accepted in their portal; once accepted we can start provisioning.
- Co-sell tagging: request it during the private-offer submission. Co-sell approval is partner-dependent and can add 1–2 weeks to the timeline, but does not block procurement.

If you lean direct MSA: 
- Standard Redwood MSA + DPA takes longer (legal redlines). To accelerate, we can push our standard healthcare addendum which covers PHI handling for managed/private deployments.
- We can still provide cloud-billed invoices under direct channel if you require it, but that requires a separate billing sponsorship setup and sometimes a reseller arrangement.

Estimated timelines:
- Marketplace private offer (no co-sell): 2–4 weeks to PO acceptance + provisioning for pilot.
- Marketplace private offer (with co-sell request): 3–6 weeks depending on partner queue.
- Direct MSA w/ DPA: 6–12 weeks depending on legal cycles and redlines.

I'll prepare two sample paths and a recommended default (marketplace private offer + Redwood DPA addendum for the pilot, then finalize MSA if you convert to production/private deployment).

—Ben Carter
Senior Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Tom Riley <tom.riley@medsynhealth.com>
To: elliot_price@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medsynhealth.com
Date: 2027-02-13T11:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Purchase options for patient-data workload (marketplace vs direct)

Thanks Elliot/Ben — that helps. A few clarifying Qs from Procurement and Legal: 
1) For the private offer + Redwood DPA addendum option, will the DPA be a separate execution outside the marketplace acceptance flow? Do we need a separate signature from Redwood?
2) If we accept marketplace billing now for the pilot, can we switch to direct MSA later without service interruption or data migration headaches?
3) Who will be Redwood's seller-of-record for the AWS private offer (Redwood or an APAC reseller)? We need to list that in the procurement request.

If you can answer those three items we can route to Legal for a greenlight to proceed with the private offer option.

Tom
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Tom Riley <tom.riley@medsynhealth.com>, elliot_price@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-14T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Purchase options for patient-data workload (marketplace vs direct)

Tom — quick answers from Legal and agreement operations: 
1) DPA integration: For AWS private offers we typically execute a DPA as a side letter (separate document) that references the private offer/order number. The marketplace acceptance handles billing; the DPA will be a Redwood signature (digital) and does not require modification of AWS terms. We'll prepare a short two-page addendum that references the PO and the services.

2) Migration/continuity: Accepting a marketplace private offer for the pilot is not a blocker to later transition to a direct MSA. We'll coordinate the changeover to ensure the same account IDs, data export procedures, and a short overlap window so there is no interruption. If you move to Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem), we'll need to schedule a cutover and execute the production SOW and acceptance criteria.

3) Seller-of-record: For US-based private offers the seller-of-record will be Redwood Inference, Inc. (we handle the private-offer creation). If you want cloud reseller billing (third-party SO R), note that has further implications for tax/invoicing. We'll list Redwood as the seller-of-record in the private-offer paperwork unless you request otherwise.

Recommended path for MedSyn pilot: 
- Create an AWS Private Offer referencing a 3-month pilot SOW (attached).
- Redwood executes a DPA side letter that references the private-offer order ID.
- Procurement provides PO number and billing sponsor; Ben will submit private offer and request co-sell tagging (optional).

I'll attach our healthcare DPA template and a short checklist of items Legal will want during the private-offer acceptance. If Procurement agrees, Ben and Elliot can kick off the private-offer creation this week.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
